description: Wageningen University & Research collected potato growth and yield observations at Lelystad and Vredepeel in the Netherlands during 2019 and 2020. The experiments vary cultivar, irrigation, nitrogen fertilisation and light interception across clayey and sandy soils. The dataset includes daily weather and soil moisture; repeated crop measurements cover photosynthesis, reflection, plant height, phenology, groundwater, biomass, leaf area, tuber number, quality and final marketability. Its named Harvard Dataverse page opened publicly at version 3.0 and lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. File metadata identifies XLSX, CSV and R files, with no displayed price. A food-supply modeller can calibrate or evaluate potato simulations for potential, water-limited and nitrogen-limited yield, including irrigation response. The two sites and two seasons do not represent all Dutch soils, cultivars or weather conditions. Measurement frequency differs across variables, and the files were not downloaded to check exact joins. This resource is related to the global potato experiment deposit G4-0565 but has a separate DOI and Netherlands trials. A previous water-sector screen rejected it as a single agronomy study; the present article documents its intended crop-model reuse.
